answers.question: What does my plan have me doing this week, and why?
answers.text:
Here is your plan for the week from Monday, August 31 to Monday, September 7. The written plan covers 1 week, with these sessions:

- Monday, August 31: 60 minutes of easy jogging
- Tuesday, September 1: 5 × (10 min jog / 2 min walk)
- Wednesday, September 2: Rest day
- Thursday, September 3: 10 × (5 min jog / 2 min walk)
- Friday, September 4: Trail leg strength (strength)
- Saturday, September 5: 72 minutes of easy jogging on a hilly trail
- Sunday, September 6: Hike 60 minutes on rolling terrain
- Monday, September 7: 45 minutes of easy jogging

Total planned jogging minutes for the week: 277 min.

Why: This is week 1 of the long-term plan's Base phase, which runs from Monday, August 31 to Monday, September 28. The phase summary says:

Base: Monday, August 31 to Monday, September 28 (4 weeks). Build the base you need for the trail race by introducing steady run and hike training plus a weekend trail session.

And the week summary says:

Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Long (run). Build the base you need for the trail race by introducing steady run and hike training plus a weekend trail session.

The plan is built on your recent weeks' mean of 318.2 min jogging minutes per week, so this week's total of 277 minutes keeps you in a steady base-building range.

answers.question: What does my plan look like over the next few months?
answers.text:
Here's what your long-term plan looks like over the next few months. It runs from Monday, August 31 to Monday, November 23, covering 12 weeks in 3 phases. You're currently in the Base phase, which started Monday, August 31 and runs through Monday, September 28. The next phase begins Tuesday, September 29. Your current week is week 1.

The phases are:

Base: Monday, August 31 to Monday, September 28 (4 weeks). Build the base you need for the trail race by introducing steady run and hike training plus a weekend trail session.

Build: Tuesday, September 29 to Monday, November 16 (7 weeks). Grow your comfort on the trails with a steady weekday climb and a longer weekend outing.

Recovery: Tuesday, November 17 to Monday, November 23 (1 week). Recover while preserving the routine you have built, so you stay ready for the next step toward race day.

Here are the weekly key sessions:

Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Long (run). Build the base you need for the trail race by introducing steady run and hike training plus a weekend trail session.

Week 2, starting Tuesday, September 8 (Base): key session Run/walk (run). Add gentle climbing and extra time on your feet to strengthen the engine for later trail work.

Week 3, starting Tuesday, September 15 (Base): key session Easy (run). Make the weekend trail session the anchor while the weekday runs develop your aerobic foundation.

Week 4, starting Tuesday, September 22 (Base): key session Long (run). Introduce more undulating terrain and practice relaxed effort over sustained climbs.

Week 5, starting Tuesday, September 29 (Build): key session Intervals (run). Grow your comfort on the trails with a steady weekday climb and a longer weekend outing.

Week 6, starting Tuesday, October 6 (Build): key session Long (run). Use back-to-back trail days to practice moving well when your legs feel heavy.

Week 7, starting Tuesday, October 13 (Build): key session Easy (run). Build durability by pairing hill work with a relaxed long session on the weekend.

Week 8, starting Tuesday, October 20 (Build): key session Strength (strength). Keep the focus on smooth effort and time outdoors as the trail race gets closer.

Week 9, starting Tuesday, October 27 (Build): key session Long (run). Practice fueling and hydration during your runs and keep every climb patient.

Week 10, starting Tuesday, November 3 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). Consolidate your fitness with consistent running and treat each climb as pacing practice.

Week 11, starting Tuesday, November 10 (Build): key session Easy (run). Sustain the training rhythm and keep the long session purposeful but relaxed.

Week 12, starting Tuesday, November 17 (Recovery): key session Recovery (run). Recover while preserving the routine you have built, so you stay ready for the next step toward race day.

This plan builds on your recent weekly jog volume of 318.2 minutes.
